# Dynamic Scene and Temporal Modeling


## Overview
Dynamic Scene and Temporal Modeling adapts static NeRF architectures to handle time-varying scenes, addressing the ghosting and blurriness artifacts that occur when static models are applied to video data [S1]. It enables novel view synthesis at arbitrary times by modeling temporal variations in geometry and appearance [G]. This family differs from static NeRF variants by explicitly incorporating temporal coordinates or deformation fields to capture scene dynamics [G].

## Shared principles
Builds on [Model Architecture Modifications](11313-model-architecture-modifications.md) [G]. All methods in this family predict volume density $\sigma$ and view-dependent color $\mathbf{c}$ for a ray $\mathbf{r}(s) = \mathbf{o} + s\mathbf{d}$ at time $t$ using the standard volume rendering integral [G]. Temporal modeling is achieved by parameterizing the scene's evolution, with specific mechanisms detailed in each child article [G].

## Subtopics

### [Gear-NeRF](13848-gear-nerf.md)
Replaces the unified 4D field with stratified "gears" (feature volumes) assigned by semantic motion scale. High-motion regions use higher-resolution sampling. Choose for object tracking and high-fidelity dynamic synthesis.

### [NeRF with Time Parameter](14705-nerf-with-time-parameter.md)
A baseline that concatenates time $t$ to the spatial input of a standard MLP. Choose for simplicity; it lacks detailed dynamic reasoning and suffers from blurriness compared to deformation-based methods.

### [Forward Warping for Novel View Synthesis](15541-forward-warping-for-novel-view-synthesis.md)
Models a static canonical field and forward warps it to target times using differentiable splatting and an inpaint network. Choose for handling many-to-one mapping difficulties in dynamic scenes.

### [Dynamic Appearance Particle Neural Radiance Field](15550-dynamic-appearance-particle-neural-radiance-field.md)
Superimposes a static grid with a dynamic particle field for monocular video. Choose for single-view dynamic reconstruction where particles model only moving elements.

### [KFD-NeRF](15551-kfd-nerf.md)
Uses a Kalman filter to combine history-based motion prediction with current observations for deformation estimation. Choose for leveraging inductive smoothness bias of deformation fields over feature interpolation.

### [SLS4D](16576-sls4d.md)
Uses sparse latent codes aggregated via attention and a deformation field. Choose for reducing parameters while maintaining high quality by abandoning direct coordinate-to-feature mapping.

### [ST-NeRF](18515-st-nerf.md)
A layered neural radiance field representation designed for editable free-viewpoint videos of dynamic scenes containing independently moving or articulated objects. Choose for spatial editing and independent manipulation of scene entities.

### ER-NeRF
A Conditional NeRF framework for effective, high-accuracy dynamic portrait creation, producing dynamic portrait videos synchronized with audio [S1]. It utilizes spatial regions' distinct contributions to steer dynamic head modeling, develops a concise and articulate Tri-Plane Hash Representation, and introduces rapid and straightforward Adaptive Pose Encoding to enhance the separation of the head and torso [S1]. Additional fine-tuning might be necessary to sustain superior rendering outcomes for poses that exceed the scope of the training dataset [S1]. It attains instantaneous rendering and rapid convergence using a compact model size [S1].

### NeRF-MS
A method that diminishes vagueness in visual alterations by implementing a ternary loss to standardize the spread of visual codes across each image [S1]. It suggests a temporary decomposition unit to more effectively distinguish still scenes from dynamic objects [S1]. It might encounter difficulties in managing significant sequence discrepancies, like severe alterations in the visual aspect of scenes caused by the activation of lights [S1]. Trials using both real-life outdoor and artificial datasets reveal that NeRF-MS attains cutting-edge results in multi-sequence scenarios, markedly enhancing rendering efficiency through the reconstruction of 3D-consistent visuals and minimizing ghost effects [S1].

### DCT-NeRF
A method that learns smooth and stable trajectories for each point in space in an input video sequence using Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) parameterization, allowing for high-quality reconstruction and consistent motion extrapolation beyond the last available frame [S2, unofficial]. It parameterizes trajectories with the Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) to model motion, and handles temporal occlusions and reflects changes in reflectance over time [S2, unofficial].

## Background
Dynamic NeRF research covers applications including indoor 3D reconstruction, portrait reconstruction, human rendering, editable interactive NeRF, and 3D perception [S1]. NeRF-MS (2023) and DP-NeRF (2023) address visual vagueness and motion blur in dynamic sequences using ternary losses and physical blur kernels [S1]. ER-NeRF (2023) and AvatarMAV (2023) focus on high-fidelity dynamic portrait and head avatar creation using conditional frameworks and motion-aware voxels [S1]. DCT-NeRF and DyBluRF utilize Discrete Cosine Transform parameterizations for smooth trajectory modeling and motion blur simulation [S2, unofficial].
